title: Locally finite type schemes as limits of finite-presentation closed models
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $f:X\to S$ a locally finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then there exist a nonempty directed set $I$, an inverse system of $S$-schemes $(X_i)$ with each $X_i\to S$ of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and each $X_i$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, closed-immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] transition maps $X_j\to X_i$ for $j\ge i$, and compatible maps $X\to X_i$, such that $(X,(X\to X_i))$ is the inverse limit in schemes [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]; every map $X\to X_i$ is a closed immersion.

proof.text: The continuous image f(X) is quasi-compact. Choose affine open neighbourhoods in S of its points and a finite subcover of this image, and let S0 be their union. Then S0 is quasi-compact, and is quasi-separated as an open subscheme of the quasi-separated S. The map f factors through f0:X→S0. This map is locally of finite type by the affine-local definition (the restriction to any affine in S0 is the same restriction as for f). By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), f0 is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Thus X and S0 satisfy the qcqs hypotheses of [def-nagata-finite-type-fp-model-system]. If X is empty take S0 empty; the same argument and construction apply.

proof.text: Over the qcqs open base S0, apply Scheme.Hom.exists_isClosedImmersion_locallyOfFinitePresentation from [lemma-nagata-finite-type-fp-model-system] to factor X→S0 as a closed immersion i:X→Y followed by a finite-presentation map q:Y→S0. Use the concrete construction Scheme.Hom.FinitePresentationApproximation.ofIsClosedImmersion q i hcomp from [def-nagata-finite-type-fp-model-system]. Its index is exactly (i.ker.FGSub)ᵒᵖ, where FGSub is [def-nagata-closed-subscheme-fp-system]. Zero gives nonemptiness and sum gives directedness. The fields of this construction give finite presentation, qcqs stages, closed transitions, closed projections and the IsLimit witness. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the stages are supplied using [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

proof.text: The open inclusion j:S0→S is locally of finite presentation: near any point of S0 choose an affine open contained in S0, also an open of S, on which j is the identity and the ring map is finitely presented. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), since S0 is qcqs and S is quasi-separated. Thus it is of finite presentation by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](d), the composites Xi→S0→S are of finite presentation. Regard the unchanged inverse diagram as S-schemes through j. Its transition maps, projections, qcqs model schemes and inverse limit in schemes are unchanged; the structural maps to S agree by composition. This proves every clause over the original, possibly non-quasi-compact S.

lean.statement: theorem exists_locallyFiniteType_limit_closed_finitePresentation {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] : ∃ (I : Type u) (_ : Preorder I), Nonempty I ∧ IsDirected I (· ≤ ·) ∧ ∃ (D : Iᵒᵖ ⥤ Scheme.{u}) (p : D ⟶ (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj S) (π : (Functor.const Iᵒᵖ).obj X ⟶ D), (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, LocallyOfFinitePresentation (p.app i) ∧ QuasiCompact (p.app i) ∧ QuasiSeparated (p.app i)) ∧ (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, CompactSpace (D.obj i) ∧ QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i)) ∧ (∀ (i j : Iᵒᵖ) (g : i ⟶ j), IsClosedImmersion (D.map g)) ∧ (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, π.app i ≫ p.app i = f) ∧ Nonempty (IsLimit (Cone.mk X π)) ∧ (∀ i : Iᵒᵖ, IsClosedImmersion (π.app i))
